title: Run several jobs at the same time with a maximum number of parallel jobs
summary: Starts one background job per file, but never more than a set number at once. When a job finishes, the next one starts. This example compresses files with gzip.

warnings: wait -n needs bash 4.3 or newer. macOS ships bash 3.2, which does not have it.
Parallel jobs share the processor and the disk. A limit that is too high can make the whole job slower, not faster.
The script does not overwrite existing .gz files. gzip reports an error for each file that already has a .gz, and the script counts it as failed. Delete the old .gz files first.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# parallel-gzip.sh - compress every file in a folder, running at most MAX_JOBS at once.
# Usage: ./parallel-gzip.sh MAX_JOBS SOURCE_DIR
# Makes NAME.gz next to each file and keeps the original (gzip -k).
# Needs bash 4.3 or newer for "wait -n".

set -euo pipefail

if (( $# != 2 )) || ! [[ $1 =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || [[ ! -d $2 ]]; then
    echo "usage: $0 MAX_JOBS SOURCE_DIR" >&2
    exit 2
fi
MAX_JOBS=$1
SRC=$2

running=0   # how many background jobs are running now
failed=0    # how many of them exited with an error

# wait_one waits until ANY one background job finishes (wait -n),
# then updates the counters.
wait_one() {
    local status=0
    wait -n || status=$?
    if (( status != 0 )); then
        failed=$((failed + 1))
    fi
    running=$((running - 1))
}

while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
    # Before starting a new job, wait while the limit is reached.
    while (( running >= MAX_JOBS )); do
        wait_one
    done
    gzip -k -- "$file" &
    running=$((running + 1))
done < <(find "$SRC" -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name '*.gz' -print0)

# Wait for the jobs that are still running at the end.
while (( running > 0 )); do
    wait_one
done

echo "all jobs finished; failed: $failed"
(( failed == 0 ))   # exit code 1 if any job failed

prerequisites: A Linux terminal with bash 4 or newer
